Proceedings under Section 207 Cr.P.C were concluded.

, prosecution has examined PW1 being the mother of the deceased and during her testimony recorded before the court she did not depose against the accused persons in terms of her FIR No.318/2022 State Vs. Rekha & Anr. PS Badarpur Page No. 27 of 30 complaint Ex.PW1/A.
31.PW2 Sagar was the husband of the deceased and PW3 was the father in law of the deceased and was therefore related to the accused persons and were interested witnesses to the cause of the accused persons.
35.Further the deceased did not leave any suicide note which could infer that she was subjected to cruelty.
All the other witnesses examined by the prosecution did not deposed regarding any of the incident by which it could be inferred that the deceased was subjected to any kind FIR No.318/2022 State Vs. Rekha & Anr.
Page No. 29 of 30 of dowry demand and the averments made on behalf of the family members of the deceased regarding demand of gold chain is also vague and general in nature and does not inspire confidence.
The net result is that above mentioned prosecution witnesses, who could have deposed about deceased Sushmita @ Sonam facing cruelty or harassment at the hands of accused persons, did not depose so, in their respective testimonies.
36.Rest of the prosecution witnesses were police officials who had done different aspects of investigation.
Their unrebutted testimonies, did not prove the aspect of "cruelty" being faced by deceased Sushmita @ Sonam, during her lifetime from accused persons.
37.Prosecution thus, failed to prove the essential ingredients of cruelty, constituting the Section 498A/304B/34 IPC.
38.So, prosecution in order to bring conviction of an accused u/sec. 306 IPC has to prove beyond reasonable doubt that accused intended to commit the said offence, by playing active role, thereby abetting victim to commit suicide.
